text: In August 2001 a corroded section of a 12-inch crude oil pipeline north of Slave Lake, Alberta, ruptured beneath a muskeg crossing and released about 80 cubic metres of oil before pressure monitoring at the pump station caught the drop. Oil pooled across roughly two hectares of wetland and a sheen reached a small creek draining toward the lake. The company brought in vacuum trucks, absorbent booms and a crew of about sixty; ducks and a beaver were found oiled. Regulators ordered the line shut until the remaining pipe had been inspected with a smart pig.

text: HAMILTON, Feb. 3, 1915 - An explosion in the gas producer house of the steel works shortly after midnight killed two men and lifted the roof clean off the building. The night foreman says a valve was being changed when the gas took fire. Workmen dug the bodies from beneath the fallen iron sheeting at daylight.
label: industrial

text: Two hundred residents of the Powell River townsite spent a night away from home in 1966 after chlorine leaked at the pulp mill; nobody was seriously hurt.
label: industrial

text: A fire in a cable vault at an Ottawa Hydro switching station on 5 March 1997 cut power to about 90,000 customers in the downtown core and the Glebe for most of the afternoon. Elevators stalled with people inside, and the federal government sent several thousand public servants home early. Crews traced the fire to an insulation breakdown on a 115-kilovolt cable.
label: industrial

text: SASKATOON, Nov. 18, 1909 - The Windsor House, the largest frame hotel in the city, was wiped out by fire in the small hours this morning, and three of the guests are known to have lost their lives. The alarm was raised by a teamster passing in the street, who saw smoke curling from the eaves. Men leaped from second-storey windows in their night clothes into the snow, and one woman was let down by a rope of knotted bed sheets. The fire brigade had trouble getting water, as the new mains are not yet extended to that part of the town. The proprietor estimates his loss at $45,000.

text: A coal-oil heater set fire to the two-room school at Elgin Ridge, west of Brandon, during the noon hour on March 2, 1949. The teacher marched forty pupils out through the cloakroom door and none was hurt, but the building and all its books were lost. Classes moved to the Orange hall for the rest of the term.

text: Several propane cylinders vented and burst during a fire at a farm supply depot on the edge of Lethbridge in May 1999. Residents within a kilometre left their homes for six hours; no one was hurt.
label: industrial

text: Penetanguishene, 1906. The tannery on the bay front was burned out; loss $60,000, sixty men idle.
label: industrial

text: An explosion inside a nitric acid unit at a chemical plant outside Medicine Hat sent an orange cloud of nitrogen dioxide drifting over the river valley on the evening of June 14, 1968. Police went through the Riverside district with loudspeakers telling people to stay inside. Eleven workers were treated for gas inhalation, and a pipe-fitter died in hospital the following week.
label: industrial

text: A 1,200-millimetre water main burst beneath Portage Avenue in Winnipeg early on 9 February 2015, tearing open a crater in the pavement and flooding the basements of several office towers. Thousands of homes in the west end lost water pressure and a boil-water advisory was issued. City crews worked in minus 30 degree weather to isolate the break, which took nineteen hours.
label: industrial

text: FREDERICTON, Dec. 1912 - The main building of the normal school was destroyed by fire this afternoon while classes were in session. The fire, which originated in the furnace room, made such headway through the old flues that the students had barely time to file out. The library, the chemical apparatus and the records of thirty years went up in the flames.
label: industrial

text: Several hundred tons of rock fell from the face of a limestone quarry near Beachville, Ont., in September 1953, burying two drillers. Both bodies were recovered the next day.
label: industrial

text: Release report, 14 April 2005: approximately 3,000 litres of sulphuric acid spilled from a transfer line at a smelter in Belledune, New Brunswick, when a gasket failed during the night shift. Part of the acid ran into a storm ditch leading to the bay before staff could dam it with sand and lime. Environment officers sampled the outfall for four days and found low pH readings near the shore, and the company was ordered to rebuild the containment around the line. No injuries were reported.
label: industrial

text: WINDSOR MILLS, Que., July 1907 - The packing house of the black powder mill exploded at a quarter past ten this morning with a roar that was heard twelve miles away. Of the six men at work in the building nothing could be found but fragments. Every pane of glass in the village was broken and plaster came down in the church. It is the third accident at the works in four years, and the people are demanding that the mill be removed to a safer distance.
label: industrial

text: The rear wall of a four-storey brick apartment block on Gottingen Street in Halifax collapsed into the lane during renovation work on the afternoon of April 11, 1972. Workmen had been removing a bearing wall in a ground-floor shop. Eighteen tenants were moved out, and one labourer was dug from the rubble with a broken back.
label: industrial

text: Underground vault fire, downtown Halifax, 2004. Some 10,000 customers without electricity for six hours; smoke drawn into two office towers.
label: industrial

text: Fire starting in the planing mill at Bracebridge on the afternoon of August 22, 1905, after six weeks without rain, spread through the lumber yard and across the street to the houses beyond. Thirty-two dwellings, a livery barn and the Baptist church were burned before a change of wind and the efforts of a bucket line saved the rest of the town.
label: industrial

text: Seven coal miners lost their lives at the Carbon Creek mine, near Hudson's Hope, B.C., on October 3, 1946, when a sudden outburst in the No. 2 seam buried the working face. The miners on the shift felt the floor heave and a gust of air and dust swept through the main haulage. Twenty-two men escaped by the return airway. Rescue teams working with picks and shovels recovered the last of the bodies five days later. The inspector of mines said that the seam had been worked under heavy cover and that warning signs of pressure had been reported to the management two weeks before.
label: industrial

text: A dust explosion in the mixing room of a commercial bakery in Mississauga at 5:15 a.m. on 21 September 2010 blew open a loading door and started a fire in the flour storage area. Three workers suffered burns. About 120 staff evacuated, and the plant remained closed for a month while the fire marshal reviewed its dust collection system.
label: industrial

text: ROSSLAND, B.C., 1902 - The opera house burned to the ground last night; the travelling company saved only its trunks.
label: industrial

text: Three hotel guests were found dead in their rooms at a Prince Albert hotel on the morning of January 21, 1965, poisoned by carbon monoxide escaping from a cracked furnace flue. Four others were taken to hospital unconscious. The coroner ordered the furnace sealed and the city began an inspection of every hotel heating plant.
label: industrial

text: Spring 1994, northern Manitoba: a dyke on the tailings pond at an abandoned copper mine was breached after the frost went out of the ground, and an estimated 20,000 cubic metres of acidic tailings slurry spilled into a creek flowing into a lake used for fishing by a nearby First Nation. Water samples showed elevated copper and zinc for several kilometres downstream. The province built an emergency berm, trucked in lime to neutralize the creek, and advised residents not to eat fish caught in the bay until further notice. A review later found the dyke had not been inspected since the mine closed.
label: industrial

text: VALLEYFIELD, Que., Oct. 1903 - The picker room of the cotton mill caught fire this morning, and before the sprinklers could do their work the flames had reached the carding floor. Some four hundred operatives, many of them girls, got out safely. Damage to machinery is heavy.
label: industrial

text: Solvent vapour ignited near a pressing machine at a Regina dry cleaning plant in 1956, and the blast burned three employees.
label: industrial

text: An explosion and fire tore through a warehouse storing consumer fireworks in an industrial park in Saint-Hyacinthe on the evening of 1 July 2001. Rockets and shells were seen bursting over the highway for nearly an hour. Firefighters held back and let the building burn while protecting the neighbouring units; two employees were treated for burns.
label: industrial

text: INVERNESS, N.S., April 1916 - Fire which broke out in the old workings of No. 1 mine has driven the men from the pit, and the management has decided to seal the slope. All the miners are accounted for except two drivers, whom it is feared were overcome by smoke near the stables. Volunteers went down three times before the heat forced them back. The horses could not be saved. Nearly 400 men are thrown out of employment until the fire is smothered, which may take months.
label: industrial

text: Falsework beneath a concrete overpass under construction on the Deerfoot Trail in Calgary gave way while a deck was being poured on August 9, 1967. Two labourers were killed and four were injured when tons of wet concrete and steel came down. An inquiry blamed inadequate bracing of the timber shoring.
label: industrial

text: Hydrofluoric acid leak, Fort Saskatchewan, 2018. Plant staff sheltered in place; one worker burned on the forearm and treated at hospital.
label: industrial

text: DAWSON, Y.T., Jan. 1905 - Fire last night destroyed a two-storey lodging house on Second Avenue and the bakery next door. An overheated stovepipe is blamed. The brigade had to thaw the hydrants with steam, and it was forty below. One lodger is missing.
label: industrial

text: Fire on the fourteenth floor of a 22-storey apartment tower in west Edmonton on 3 February 2007 forced hundreds of residents into the corridors in the middle of the night. A smoking-related fire in a living room spread to the balcony and broke windows, and smoke entered the stairwells because two fire doors had been propped open. Firefighters carried down several elderly tenants; one woman on the fifteenth floor died of smoke inhalation and 17 people were treated for smoke exposure. With temperatures near minus 25, transit buses were parked outside as warming shelters. The building was declared unfit for occupancy for three weeks while fire and smoke damage were repaired.
